page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v5 is an ARM64-based server powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2458 GB SSD, and the platform is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks. The server achieved a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and software compilation with Clang. Redis SET operations also performed in the top tier, reaching 84.83 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores falling into the lower tier. Large-model LLM prompt processing also shows weaker performance.

Given its ARM architecture and low memory-to-core ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for highly parallelized workloads that do not require high memory capacity per thread. It is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, Redis-based caching, and web serving. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded tasks due to the 2.0 GB per core limit and lower single-core benchmark ratings.
